messages:
support-ops: FYI: NimbusGames just escalated — p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~450ms to ~1.2s in us-west around 02:10PT. Support ticket #4521 and screenshots attached https://support.redwood.example/t/4521 :red_circle:

jess: Got it; I'm oncall. Do we have alert that fired?

sre-bot: Alert: high_p99_latency /v1/generate us-west — p99 > 1s for 5m (fired at 1934567800)

omar: I pulled their traces, most tail traces show a few 1s spikes, but our dashboard p99 panel is only at ~320ms. Dashboard vs raw histogram mismatch.

lia: Can you paste the dashboard panels? I bet one is a rolled-up recording rule and the other is a histogram panel backed by raw histograms.

omar: Panel A (top) is a timeseries of recording rule redwood:service:api_p99:rate5m (Prometheus) — shows 320ms. Panel B is a histogram heatmap/query that shows spikes into 1s+ buckets.

jess: That's the classic rollup vs histogram problem. Which rule is the p99 rule using?

lia: Paste the rule and the histogram query.

omar: Rule:

```
- record: redwood:service:api_p99:rate5m
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```

Histogram panel query (raw):

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api",route="/v1/generate",region="us-west"}[5m])) by (le))
```

lia: Hm looks same but note the rule didn't have a region label; the rule aggregates across all regions. If other regions are much lower latency the global rollup will pull the percentile down.

dmitri: But expansion across regions shouldn't make global p99 lower than region p99 that had spike. Are we sure the rule's vector matching and label sets are consistent?

omar: I checked — the rule loses the region label because of the grouping in the sum() by (le). The recording rule is defined without preserving region, so it produces a global p99. The metric we show on the timeseries panel is that recording rule (global), while the histogram panel filters to region=us-west.

jess: That explains discrepancy. So the alert engine fired on a per-region metric or global? support-ops, what fired the customer alert?

support-ops: The customer's SDK reported increased latency and opened the ticket. Our internal alert that bumped the support queue was the per-region alert created by a local NimbusGames script hitting our /metrics endpoint (customer-run). We also had a synthetic check for us-west that showed elevated p99.

maria: Two actions: 1) We need an immediate mitigation for the customer (workaround) 2) Fix observability so dashboards/alerts are consistent.

jess: Mitigation ideas: route traffic for that customer to a less loaded instance/variant, or temporarily scale up dedicated pool for that tenant. Can we do a quick traffic split?

omar: For NimbusGames they're on shared hosted capacity. We can pin them to a different model variant with lower tail latency for a short window. That requires a config change: update routing policy for org:nimbusgames to prefer model v2-quick for 30m. I can do that if approved.

dmitri: Before switching, check whether KV cache warmness is the cause: traces show cache miss ratio higher for their requests in the spike window. If it's cache coldness crawling, switching model might not help.

lia: Also, we should change the recording rule to preserve region label and create region-scoped p99 rules to avoid future confusion. Proposed rule tweak:

```
- record: redwood:service:api_p99:rate5m:by_region
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (region, le))
```

Then update dashboards to use the by_region recording rule when scoped.

jess: Agreed. Omar, proceed with routing change + notify support. Lia, make the recording rule change and patch dashboards. Dmitri, confirm cache metrics.

omar: Starting routing change now. Command I'm running:

```
redwoodctl route update --org nimbusgames --route /v1/generate --prefer-model v2-quick --duration 30m
```

I'll post when done.

dmitri: Checked cache stats: KV cache hit-rate for nimbusgames dev keyspace dropped from 95% -> 62% during spike window. Also noticed a recent config rollout that shortened cache TTL from 10m to 30s for small request prefixes (PR #6085 landed 1934567000). That likely caused cold-key amplification.

jess: Oof. Who merged PR 6085?

maria: That was me; I changed TTL to reduce memory during tests. I didn't realize it would apply to prod prefixes. I'll revert the TTL patch in a minute.

support-ops: Customer is confirming improved response times after a few minutes — reporting fewer timeouts.

omar: Routing change applied successfully. New traffic split active.

lia: I pushed a fix to recording rules and a patch to the dashboard panels so they're consistent (changed to use by_region rule and added panel help text). PR: https://git.redwood.example/dashboards/patches/1352

dmitri: Maria's TTL revert is merged to canary; rolling to prod now. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/cache-service TTL=600 --namespace prod` (will take ~2m to warm).

jess: Any residual alerts?

sre-bot: Alert resolved: high_p99_latency /v1/generate us-west — resolved (at 1934568110)

support-ops: NimbusGames says p99 is back to ~420ms and they're happy for now. They asked what caused it — can we draft a short RCA blurb for them?

maria: Draft for customer: short summary — transient cache TTL regression after a recent config change led to increased cache misses for some prefixes, causing elevated tail latency for a subset of requests in us-west. We rolled back TTL, applied temporary routing to a lower-tail variant, and updated observability to prevent alert/dashboard mismatch. Follow-ups: internal postmortem and config gating.

jess: Add follow-ups: add unit tests to prevent TTL changes from affecting prod prefixes, and add alert mapping doc explaining differences between recording rules and raw histograms.

dmitri: I'll run a quick sweep for other tenants affected by PR #6085 and open follow-up tickets.

lia: Note for the team: When building dashboards, prefer region-scoped recording rules or include explicit label matching to avoid global aggregation surprises. Also add a dashboard tooltip clarifying which metric is aggregated at what label set.

jess: Great work everyone. I'll close the incident after we have the short RCA and the TTL follow-up ticket. :white_check_mark:
